messages.content: "331 :     protected abstract void iterateSimplex(final Comparator<RealPointValuePair> comparator)\n332 :         throws FunctionEvaluationException, OptimizationException, IllegalArgumentException;"

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test exercises
  - The test constructs a function with multiple local/global extrema and uses MultiDirectional to minimize it starting from [-3.0, 0] with a 2D start configuration [0.2, 0.2]. It sets a strict convergence checker and bounds the iterations. It then asserts the optimizer converges to the expected local minimum with a reasonable number of evaluations.

- Reported symptom
  - The issue report states that MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex loops forever when the starting point is already the correct solution.

- How the algorithm is supposed to work
  - A “direct search” optimizer typically:
    - Builds a simplex around the current best point.
    - Tries reflection, possibly expansion, or contraction.
    - If no improvement is achieved, it shrinks the simplex or declares convergence.
    - It performs a single “iteration” and returns control to the outer optimize loop where convergence is checked.

- What the code does instead
  - MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex(comparator) contains an internal while (true) loop and only returns when one of two strict improvement conditions holds:
    - Reflection improves over the current best (comparator.compare(reflected, best) < 0), in which case it may accept either the reflected or expanded simplex and returns.
    - Contraction improves over the current best (comparator.compare(contracted, best) < 0), in which case it returns.
  - There is no branch for the “no improvement” case. If neither reflection nor contraction strictly improves upon best, the loop body finishes and immediately restarts (still inside iterateSimplex), with no state change that can alter the outcome.

- Why this can loop forever at the correct solution (or a degenerate/flat simplex)
  - evaluateNewSimplex builds a transformed simplex around the current best point: x_transformed = x_smallest + coeff * (x_smallest - x_original).
  - If the simplex has collapsed (e.g., all vertices equal to the best point), then for any coeff (reflection with 1.0 or contraction with gamma), every transformed point equals the best point again. That is, the reflected and contracted simplexes are identical to the original one.
  - The comparator sees reflected == best and contracted == best, so both strict-improvement checks fail.
  - Because iterateSimplex lacks an “else” branch for this case and does not check convergence inside the loop, it repeats the loop endlessly. The comment “// check convergence” present in the contracted branch is not implemented, confirming the missing termination logic.
  - Furthermore, iterateSimplex is supposed to perform exactly one “iteration” and return so the outer optimization loop can check convergence; the while (true) prevents this and traps control inside iterateSimplex until strict improvement occurs, which may never happen at the optimum.

- Relation to the failing test
  - The test uses a starting point with y = 0 where the function is defined to return 0 (a flat/plateau condition along axes). Depending on the constructed initial simplex, it is possible for reflections and contractions to not strictly improve the best point (especially near a plateau or at an exact optimum), triggering the “no improvement” path that currently has no exit, which can cause non-termination or iteration/evaluation counts to fall outside the expected range.
  - Even if the test’s starting point is not exactly the global optimum, this flawed loop logic means iterateSimplex may get stuck whenever neither reflection nor contraction strictly beats the current best, violating the algorithm’s need to either shrink, accept equality as convergence, or return control for convergence checking.

- Root cause
  - MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex contains an unconditional while (true) with no exit path in the “no improvement” case. At exact optima or degenerate simplexes (or plateaus causing equality), both reflection and contraction fail to strictly improve; because there is no shrink/no-improvement handling and no convergence check inside the loop, iterateSimplex loops indefinitely.
  - The presence of a placeholder comment “// check convergence” inside the contraction branch further evidences that the convergence/termination logic is missing.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
